text:
Cole Perfetti is breaking out at 24, and the role change is the reason. He's playing 18:10 a night, up from 15:37, and he's on the ice for 90% of Winnipeg's power-play time, against 50% last season. The result: 18 points in 20 games, nearly double last year's pace, eight of them on the power play, and a four-game point streak through the Jets' five-game winning run.

What makes it believable is that his own chances grew with it, to 1.47 expected goals per 60 from 1.08, and he's shooting 12.1%, a touch below league average. If anything, he's been a little unlucky as a finisher. Winnipeg is also nearly seven points better in five-on-five chance share with him than without. His point rate is running above our talent range, so expect a bit of a slowdown there.

Evolving-Hockey liked his defense last season more than his offense, 95th percentile at taking chances away. If that two-way game sticks with the bigger minutes, the Jets have a real top-six forward.
headline: Perfetti is having the year Winnipeg waited for
